analyst_view.overall: Early view: Slovan Bratislava are bottom with no points and, under Yaya Toure, hold an unwanted record for consecutive Champions League defeats after losing 4-0 at LASK. Real Betis (11th, 9 points) lost 2-1 at Borussia Dortmund on matchday 4 and need the win to stay in the race for the top eight; Manuel Pellegrini's side should control this game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and I lean a little higher. Slovan conceded four in the first half and early second half at LASK, and their defensive record in this competition is the worst of the 36. Betis scored in Dortmund through Aitor Ruibal and have enough creativity, with Isco and Antony, to score several.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and I stay with it. Betis should have most of the ball and win most of the corners, but if they score early the game may lose its intensity. Nothing I found argues strongly either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Betis picked up five yellow cards in Dortmund, but that was a tight away game against a strong side; here they should be in control. Slovan had two players booked at LASK. The two effects cancel, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, which already reflects Betis's expected dominance. Slovan created little at LASK, so almost all the volume depends on Betis, which makes a figure above 31 hard to support. I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Betis should test the Slovan goalkeeper often, but the hosts' own contribution will be small. I see no reason to move away from the estimate.
